steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
To make the fruit layer: Mix strawberries, rhubarb, white sugar, and flour together in a large bowl. Place the mixture in a 9x13-inch baking dish.

To make the crisp topping: Combine 1 ½ cups flour, brown sugar, oats, and butter and mix until crumbly. You may want to use a pastry cutter for this. Sprinkle on top of the rhubarb and strawberry layer.
Bake in the preheated oven until crisp and lightly browned, about 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Rhubarb Crisp
raw_recipe.description: This delightful strawberry rhubarb crisp has a layer of sweet and tangy fruit topped with a buttery oat topping baked until golden and crisp.

video.description: In this video, we'll show you what to do with an abundance of rhubarb and strawberries. We add a little bit of sugar, flour, and butter and bake this homey, delicious dessert with a crisp topping.

review.reviewBody: This recipe in itself deserves 4 stars, however, when tweaked a bit, the results are 10 stars! I used 4 cups of strawberries (roughly a pound and a half) and 4 cups of rhubarb (5 long stalks), 5 Tbsp flour and 3/4 cup of sugar. I probably could have used even less sugar. Bottom line is, if your strawberries are fresh and ripe, you really don't need that much sugar. I will likely try 1/2 cup next time. Then I poured the fruit mixture into a 10 x 15 1/2 bar pan. I did not adjust the topping-- I made as the recipe called for and there was more than enough to cover the top. I baked for the same amount of time and at the same temp and it came out perfect! (just be sure to put aluminum foil down in your oven because the juices run over the side of the bar pan!) This recipe will easily serve 12 and is absolutely the perfect combination of sweetness, tartness and crunchiness. Great summer recipe!

This is an excellent recipe - easy, fast and very good. I used a larger (10 X 14) dish and increased the fruit to about 5 cups for each. I could have used even more. I used slightly less than 1 c. white sugar and 4-5 tbs of flour for the fruit. I also added the zest of one juicing orange, a teaspoon of cinnamon and a few grates of nutmeg - all of which made a big impact on the taste. For the topping, I made the amount noted in the recipe, but did not use it all - and that was on a significantly bigger batch. Just use what looks right. I did not change the baking time. Good luck!

I followed others' suggestions and halved the butter, flour (used whole wheat flour) and sugars. To thicken the fruit, I used Tapioca instead of flour (3 Tbsp). Also, I added 1/2 Tbsp of Apple Pie Spice in the oat mixture. Cooked 30 minutes - it was fantastic!

After reading all the comments, I used 4 cups each of strawberries and rhubarb. Used 5 tbsp. flour and only 1/2 cup of sugar to add to the fruit as my berries were freshly picked and very sweet. I added 1 tsp cinnamon and 2/3 cups walnuts to the topping. I only cooked it for 35 minutes. It was delicious!!

I cut the recipe in half and put it in an 8 x 8” glass baking dish. It was absolutely delicious! Not too tart. If you want a little more tart, then add a little less sugar. The topping was crunchy and sweet. I would probably do a little less than half of the topping recipe for the 8 x 8“ dish. Adding some blueberries to the recipe might also be really good. This is definitely one I will be making again!
I only had enough rhubarb for 1/2 a recipe, so I cut recipe in half and baked in 9 x 9 pan. It was just perfect exactly as written. Next week at the farmer's market I'll pick up double the rhubarb!

I used the top reviewer's tip and used 5 tablespoons of flour and increased the fruit to 4 and 4 cups each. It was the right consistency for spooning into dishes. And I like this amount of topping. What the topping is missing is a bit of salt and vanilla. I added a half teaspoon of kosher salt, and next time might add a whole teaspoon.
My husband is diabetic, so I substituted 1/2 of Truvia Cane Sugar Blend for the white sugar. I also only had 1/2 c of butter, so I substituted 1/2 of coconut oil. Came out YUMMY!
I used 2 lbs of strawberries and 2 lbs of rhubarb. All other ingredients stayed the same. Turned out wonderful. Not too sweet and not too sour. Just right. It’s in my favorites. Thanks!!
My family loved this. Like others suggested I made 1/2 the crumb and only used 3/4 cup sugar like others. I also used 4 cups strawberry and 6 cup rhubarb. It was wonderful.
For the crumb topping I used 1/2 C. of butter instead of 1 C. It was a lighter topping and fewer calories. Other than that it was fantastic.

The ratio of fruit to topping is way off. There is not enough fruit. All I could taste was the topping. The fruit was hidden in this recipe. I would double the amount of fruit next time. The sweetness was OK for me, but I do like sweetness.
very tasty! Prepared this for Muths and Kurz and everyone loved it. Used less sugar.
Too much sugar! Too much butter! Too much topping. I added a sprinkle of fresh lemon juice. The recipe was very tasty but too sweet.

Based on others’ notes, I went with four cups of each and 5 T flour (my strawberries came from the garden and were very ripe and juicy). I also added 1/3 C+ chopped walnuts to topping and reduced butter by 3-ish T. Delicious and the fruit was not runny (an issue, I think, with a lot of crisp recipes). I didn’t have an orange, but like the suggestion of orange zest someone mentioned—will try that next time. Also plan to add vanilla next time—forgot. Great recipe.

I used 1/2 cup of monk fruit sweetener that I need to use up. I only had coconut flour and homemade granola. I served it with French vanilla ice cream, and I enjoyed the flavour. I would make this again but might add a little more coconut flour.
This was the perfect amount of sweet and tart. Everyone loved it!
Did not work for me. I think it’s way too much sugar and way too much topping. Too much flour in the topping so it was not “crisp”.
Easy to follow and delicious results.

There is nothing I would change with this recipe. It comes our so wonderful every time. I am probably pretty loose with the amount (I go over on both fruits). I also bake it in a cast iron skillet which caramelizes the fruits and sugars beautifully.
